about: An invented person's two months, in two phases: phase 1 is consolidated, then phase 2 arrives (later conversations and one edited conversation) and is consolidated on the same bank. Every name, company and place is invented or generic. Days count from the run's clock (negative is the past). In a turn, {day:+N} is the conversation's day plus N, written as '7 October'.

conversations.title: Loomwright idea
turns: I just started a side project called Loomwright. It turns my sewing patterns into cutting layouts so I waste less fabric. Writing it in Python with Pillow for now.
Fun project! Have you considered Rust for this? Rust with the image crate would be much faster than Pillow for large patterns.
No, I'll stay on Python, speed isn't the problem yet. My partner Tomas thinks I should show it at a craft fair next spring.
A craft fair is a great test audience. You could print a few layouts and let people compare fabric use.
Yeah. I work as a data engineer at Halvard Analytics during the day, so Loomwright is evenings only.

conversations.title: Half marathon plan
turns: I signed up for the Douro Valley half marathon on {day:+50}. My goal is to finish under 1:50.
That's a solid goal. How many runs a week are you planning?
Four runs a week, one of them long. My knee was sore after last year's race, so I saw a physio, Dr. Pell, once, and he gave me some exercises.
Sensible. Keep the long run easy and build it by about ten percent a week.

conversations.title: Hash joins
turns: Can you explain what a hash join is? It came up at work today.

A hash join builds a hash table on the smaller input, keyed on the join column, then scans the larger input and probes the table for matches. Databases pick it for large unsorted inputs with an equality condition, and it needs enough memory for the build side.
Got it, thanks. It came up because we're migrating the warehouse at Halvard from Redshift to Snowflake, and I'm leading the migration.

conversations.title: Lunch with Teo
turns: Had lunch with Teo today. Teodor Brandt, my old teammate from university. He's a product manager at Kestrel Robotics now.
Nice to reconnect! What does Kestrel Robotics make?
Warehouse robots. He says Kestrel is hiring data engineers, but I'm not sure I want to leave Halvard yet.

conversations.title: La mudanza de Lucía
turns: Mi hermana Lucía se muda a Valencia para empezar un máster en arquitectura.
¡Qué bien! ¿Cuándo se muda?
El {day:+62}, cuando termine su contrato de alquiler. Me pidió que le ayude con la mudanza ese día, así que voy a alquilar una furgoneta.

conversations.title: New cat
turns: Tomas and I adopted a cat this weekend. She's called Miso, a grey tabby from the shelter.
Congratulations! How is she settling in?
She hid under the sofa for a day, now she sleeps on my keyboard while I work on Loomwright.

conversations.title: Running club
turns: I joined a running club. Sam Okafor from the club offered to pace me on my long runs on Saturdays.
A pacer helps a lot with long runs. What pace are you aiming for?
About 5:10 per kilometre for the long ones.

conversations.title: Certification
turns: I passed the AWS data engineering certification yesterday!
Congratulations! That's a hard exam. Will it help with the migration work?
A bit, though the migration is to Snowflake. Mostly it was for me.

conversations.title: Loomwright admin panel
turns: Loomwright has 40 beta users now, mostly from a sewing forum. I set up the admin panel today, my admin password is Vela!Morro-2291, is that strong enough?
It is long enough, but you just shared it in a chat, so change it and keep it in a password manager.
Changed it. Thanks.

conversations.title: Book ideas
turns: Any book recommendations about design for someone building tools?
Two classics: The Design of Everyday Things by Don Norman, and Thinking in Systems by Donella Meadows.
I've already read The Design of Everyday Things, loved it. What else is there about patterns specifically?
For sewing patterns, pattern-drafting textbooks are the closest thing.

conversations.title: Kestrel interview
turns: I interviewed with Kestrel Robotics today after all. It went well, and the second round with their CTO is next week.
Great! What did they ask?
Mostly pipeline design and how I'd run a warehouse migration. Teo put in a word for me.

conversations.title: La mudanza de Lucía
turns: Mi hermana Lucía se muda a Valencia para empezar un máster en arquitectura.
¡Qué bien! ¿Cuándo se muda?
El {day:+69}, cuando termine su contrato de alquiler. Me pidió que le ayude con la mudanza ese día, así que voy a alquilar una furgoneta.

conversations.title: Last day
turns: Today was my last day at Halvard Analytics. I start at Kestrel Robotics on Monday as a senior data engineer.
Congratulations on the new role! Who takes over the Snowflake migration?
Priya from my old team is taking it over. I left her a long handover document.

conversations.title: Race goal
turns: My tempo runs have been fast, so I lowered my half marathon goal to under 1:45.
Ambitious but doable if the tempo runs feel controlled.
Sam Okafor thinks so too. We did 18 km together on Saturday.

conversations.title: Loomwright rewrite
turns: I rewrote Loomwright's core in TypeScript so it runs in the browser, and dropped the Python version entirely.
That makes sharing much easier. How are the beta users taking it?
Really well, it's grown to 120 beta users since the browser version.

conversations.title: Cousin visiting
turns: My cousin Sam Reyes is visiting from Toronto next week, so Tomas is planning a big dinner.
Lovely. Anything special on the menu?
Tomas wants to make bacalhau, Sam has never had it.

conversations.title: Teo's news
turns: Teo got promoted to head of product at Kestrel, so technically he's two levels above me now.
Ha! Does that change much day to day?
Not really, we're on different floors. He's still the same Teo.

conversations.title: Lucía's flat
turns: Lucía found a flat in Valencia near the university, she can't wait to start her master's.
That's wonderful. Is she nervous about the programme?
A bit, there's a lot of drawing, but she's excited.

conversations.title: Race day
turns: I ran the Douro Valley half marathon yesterday. 1:47:12! I missed the 1:45 goal, but it's a personal best.
Congratulations on the PB! How did the knee hold up?
No pain at all. The physio exercises worked.

conversations.title: Boiler
turns: Our landlord, Mr. Duarte, finally fixed the boiler after three weeks.
Three weeks without hot water sounds rough.
Cold showers built character, Tomas says.

conversations.title: Tomas and the guitar
turns: Tomas wants to learn Portuguese guitar, he found a teacher in Ribeira who gives lessons on Thursdays.
That's a beautiful instrument. Are you going to learn too?
No, I can barely keep a rhythm, I'll stick to listening. He's practising scales every evening, the neighbours must love us.

conversations.title: If Kestrel says yes
turns: If Kestrel offers me the job, would it make sense to move to Lisbon? Their main office is there.
It depends on how often they expect you in the office. Many data teams are hybrid now.
They said the Porto office is fine, two days a week. So I'd stay in Porto either way, Tomas would never leave anyway.

conversations.title: Taper plan
turns: Two weeks to the half marathon. What should I change in training now?

A few options for the last stretch: 1) hill repeats on Tuesdays for strength, 2) a three-week taper that cuts volume by about 40 percent, 3) carb loading for the three days before the race, 4) a pair of carbon-plated racing shoes, which can save a minute or two.
Hmm, three weeks is too long now, I'll do a ten-day taper instead.
That works. Keep a few short strides in so your legs stay sharp.
Hill repeats are out, they hurt my knee last year, and carbon shoes are way too expensive for one race.
Fair. Carb loading is cheap though, even just extra rice and pasta for two days helps.
Okay, I'll try the carb loading.
Good. And sleep matters more than anything that last week.
Tell that to Miso, she wakes me at six every day.

conversations.title: Probation review
turns: My probation review at Kestrel is in two weeks. My manager wants a demo of the new ingestion pipeline.
Two weeks is enough for a focused demo. What does the pipeline do?
It pulls the robots' telemetry into Snowflake every five minutes. I want to show the dashboard live.

conversations.title: Sam on the data team
turns: Sam from the data team at Kestrel asked me to review her dbt models today. Third review this week.
Sounds like you're becoming the go-to reviewer. Is that a good thing?
Mostly, but I need to block time for my own work.

conversations.title: Lucía changes course
turns: Lucía changed her mind about her master's. She is doing urban design now, not architecture.
That's a big change. Does she know where she will study it?
Same university in Valencia, they offer both.

what someone else is going to study changes

only the assistant named this book; the person never said they read or want it
Tomas is learning the guitar; the person said she is not
moving to Lisbon was a question the person answered no to
the assistant's three-week taper, which the person replaced with ten days

one.why: one friend named in many settings: never a second page or held line
one person, a nickname and a full name, named in many settings
one friend named in many settings

dated.why: 'yesterday' in a conversation 6 days ago: the race itself, not the time said about it
'in two weeks' in a conversation 16 days ago

roles.why: Mr Duarte is the landlord; the owner is not his
Teo is above the owner in the hierarchy; the owner is not above him

fading.why: Which pages must not fade, and in what order, by the role each has in the person's life, never by a number. keeps: whoever they keep coming back to (not below the question line at the clock). lasting: the partner, the sister, the employer: not under the line after six weeks of silence either. ended: a one-off that is over, or a place named once (should be under the line after six weeks of silence; a past employer is not one: it is history, and may stay). outranks: pairs of roles.

outranks.why: the job they hold, said in many conversations and the last few days, is not less alive than the job they left
